text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Philips Electronics finds anonymous buyer for 26.6 pct of
its 31.6 pct stake in ailing German consumer electronics
company Grundig. (p1)
- Dutch trade with Poland and Russia increasingly hindered
by floods in Eastern Europe. (p1)
- Kitchenware and bicycle maker Atag sees 1997 first half
profit plunge, but is confident about second half results. (p3)
- Parliament to question minister of Overseas Development on
decision to stop export subsidies to developing countries. (p5)
- Investments in Dutch commercial property increased four-
fold to Dfl 3.2 bn in the first half of 1997. (p15)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- The number of social benefit frauds appears to have
diminished by one third in the past two years. (p1)
- Transhipment consortium Deka/ECT seeks to continue
bankrupt Bell Lijn with 99 of 153 jobs. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- The CIA tried to infiltrate the Dutch Labour party (PvdA)
in the seventies and eighties. (p3)
TROUW
- Philips Electronics shies away from dubious business
climate of commercial television and new media. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Realty fund Capa City, eyed by rival Uni-Invest, books Dfl
8.1 (5.5) million return on investment in first half of 1997. (p8)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
